shipped_rows.title_o: The Benefit of Becoming Friends: Complaining after Service Failures Leads Customers with Strong Ties to Increase Loyalty

blind_target.evidence_quote: Claim for Review – The claim selected was that strongly tied customers who complain (vs. withhold feedback) after a service failure will increase their loyalty. In contrast, for weakly tied customers, complaining has no effect on loyalty.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Stage 2: H* was not supported as the interaction term on the overall ANOVA was not significant. In addition, the pattern of means in the strong ties group was not consistent but the pattern of means in the weak ties group was consistent.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Both completed stages explicitly reject support for the focal interaction. A consistent weak-ties mean pattern is ancillary to the central failed test. The final report identifies the target by project shorthand, but supplies no reference entry.

luna_triage.reason: The final report names the project as Umashankar_JournMarket_2017 and states the focal finding: customers with strong trainer ties who complain after service failure should show increased intended loyalty. The supplied 2017 Umashankar, Ward, and Dahl row is the matching original; it represents the same tie-strength and complaint loyalty finding.
